name: verify-tools
// tags: type:tooling since OR-35: the production preflight (tools/verify/preflight) runs the ecs-core domain through tools/seed/load-domain.mjs, so this project reads the typed core the way seed-tools does
// test: The runners here (the initial-bundle guard, the P0 proofs) keep their pure parts in node:test specs, so `test` is node's own runner rather than vitest; the runners themselves need a build or the emulators and run as `pnpm run verify:bundle` and `pnpm run verify:p0`. Its inputs reach past tools/verify because the preflight's spec reads the repository: the functions' source (P7's and P8's real-tree pins), firebase.json and package.json (the deploy wiring), tools/seed/load-domain.mjs (imported by the preflight), firestore.indexes.json (the audit-index spec's pins, tools/verify/indexes) and the TypeScript compiler P7 and P8 parse with — a cache keyed on tools/verify alone would replay a stale pass
// layering: Law 8 (CLAUDE.md): tier hierarchy, import cycles, tier barrels and the root-barrel ban in libs/ecs-core, deep relative imports across libs/apps/tools. It reads the whole workspace in about a second, so it is never cached: a cached pass could hide a new violation in a project it does not depend on
